To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the microsomal triacygylcerol lipase activity is stimulated by Mn2+, has a pH optimum of 6, and is inactivated by pronase.
we have identified a microsomal enzyme that hydrolyzes cholesteryl esterse and triacylglycerols and that is not inhibited by cobalt acetate.

the microsomal (non-lysosomal) triacylglyceride lipase and cholesterol esterase activities in rat liver were distinguished by their sensitivity to cobalt acetate, pH optimum, and solubilization by osmotic disruption.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a sensitive assay for microsomal triacyglycerol lipase activity in rat liver and human fibroblast homogenates.

the development of assays that distinguish between microsomal and lysosomal triacyglycerol lipase and cholesterol esterase activities and with the subcellular localization of these activities in rat liver and human fibroblast cells.
the characterization of the microsomal enzymes involved in the metabolism of triacylglycerols and cholesteryl oleate in the rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Mn2+ stimulated triacylglycerols and cholesteryl-ester hydrolases in rat liver and in fibroblastic cell culture are microsomal in nature, and are not lysosomal.
the Mn2+ stimulated triacylglyceride lipase and cholesterly esterase activities are located in the microsomal fraction of rat liver.
the microsomal triacyglycerol lipase activity is not the same as the lysosomal activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Mn2+ stimulated triacylglyceride lipase and cholesteroyl ester hydrolase activities in the liver are microsomal in location.
the Mn2+ stimulated triacylglycerols lipase and cholesterols esterase activities are microsomal in origin, while the activities that were not stimulated by Mn2+ are lysosomal.
the microsomal activities are not lysosomal and that they are not the same as the lysosomal tri-acylglycerol or cholesteryl estase activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the triacylglyceride lipase activity in liver microsomes was not inhibited by cobalt acetate, whereas the lysosomal tri-acylglyceride activity was.
the microsomal triacyl glycerol lipase and the cholesteryl estase are different from the lysosomal ones.
we have developed a method to separate the microsomal from the lysosomal activities of the enzymes triacylglyceride lipase and cholesterolesterase.
